statement: The normative format specification is a Core-tier deliverable; without it there is only an implementation, not a format.
The conformance corpus plus standalone verifier is a Core-tier deliverable (detailed in §19.3).
The CLI is Core tier, described as the product's face and the only surface most users touch.
research_needed: Usability/adoption evidence that most users interact only via CLI (vs. library, CI plugin, file manager).

statement: The core library comprising model, planner and container is Core tier.
A read-only, minimal-dependency format/parser library is Core tier (rationale in §19.2).
Adapter packages for ZIP, the tar family and stream codecs are Core tier because adoption depends on them (§21).
refines_or_supersedes: Consistent with §14.4 Tier 1 adapter set L1644-1653 (ZIP, tar family, gzip, zstd, xz, bzip2)

statement: Codec and transform plugins are Ecosystem tier and registry-gated (§5.8).
Language bindings are Ecosystem tier, not Core.
FUSE / mount integration is Ecosystem tier, not Core.
Build-system and CI integrations are Ecosystem tier even though the table rates them high adoption leverage (§21).
research_needed: Evidence of which build/CI integrations drive archive-format adoption.
decision_needed: Given Stage 2 depends on CI/build plugins, will any first-party integration ship with v1 despite Ecosystem tiering?

statement: Package-manager integrations are Ecosystem tier and belong to adoption Stages 4-5.
The format library must be a read-only, minimal-dependency parser and verifier deliberately separated from the core library that contains the planner, adapters and writer.
research_needed: Dependency-graph audit showing the reader crate excludes planner/adapters/writer.
decision_needed: What are the crate/package boundaries and permitted dependencies of the minimal reader?

statement: Reading has a smaller security surface than writing and far smaller than adapting; software that only consumes archives should not have to link a ZIP parser.
research_needed: Fuzzing and attack-surface measurement of reader vs writer vs adapters; link-graph check.

statement: The minimal reader is the artifact that must survive thirty years; a small reader with a bounded dependency set can be rebuilt from the specification by a future implementer, whereas a monolith cannot.
research_needed: Clean-room reimplementation exercise from spec alone; dependency longevity analysis.

statement: The minimal reader must decode the baseline codec set within its 'stated size budget', but neither §19.2 nor §20.6 states any numeric size budget (only an analogy to a <=1 MB decompressor).
refines_or_supersedes: Inconsistent with §4.9 L479 which says §20.6 'sets an explicit budget'; §20.6 L2245 gives only an analogy
research_needed: Measure decoder size of candidate baseline codecs (LOC, binary size, dependency count).
decision_needed: What is the minimal reader's size budget, in what unit, and how is it measured and enforced?

statement: Baseline codec set size is disciplined by the reader: if the minimal reader cannot decode the baseline set within its size budget, the baseline set is too large.
refines_or_supersedes: Links to §20.6 L2245 and §25.1 item 3 (baseline codec set deferred)
research_needed: Decoder-size measurements for candidate codecs.
decision_needed: Which codecs form the baseline set under the size budget?

statement: Shipping a conformance corpus as a core v1 deliverable is described as the specification's clearest departure from normal archive-format practice.
research_needed: Survey of whether other formats ship official conformance corpora (cf. matrix L2376).

statement: Prior research found an external, licence-clean, multi-format archive conformance corpus with an accept/iffy/malicious/reject taxonomy already exists and has exactly one known consumer.
evidence_in_source: prior research programme (Research III, cited at §26.1 L2589); corpus unnamed here
research_needed: Re-verify corpus identity, licence and current consumer count with primary citation.

statement: A major package registry vendored a subset of that corpus, collapsed its four classes into two, and promoted two upstream-malicious cases into its own accept class.
evidence_in_source: prior research programme (Research III); registry unnamed
research_needed: Primary citation (repository path/commit) and check whether still present.

statement: On the promoted cases, six implementations produce five different results, including a content substitution where both readings pass their checksum.
research_needed: Reproduce with current implementation versions; record in observed-outcome matrix.

statement: Absent a normative conformance suite, every gatekeeper builds a private one and the private ones disagree.
research_needed: Survey of gatekeeper validators (registries, scanners) and their disagreement rates.

statement: Entrybound ships a versioned corpus of conformance cases, each with a stable ID, minimal bytes generated from format primitives, the property under test, a specification reference, and an expectation class.
decision_needed: What is the case metadata schema and ID scheme?

statement: Corpus expectation classes are REQUIRED, FORBIDDEN, ACCEPTABLE and PROFILE_DEPENDENT, plus UNRESOLVED.
The UNRESOLVED expectation class must be empty for the native format; an unresolved case in Entrybound's own corpus is a specification bug.
research_needed: Corpus coverage audit against every normative rule.

statement: UNRESOLVED cases are permitted and expected in adapter corpora, where genuine legacy ambiguity lives.
Ship an observed-outcome matrix recording, for every case, what each implementation actually does.
refines_or_supersedes: §25.1 item 22 L2554 derives --compat models from this matrix
research_needed: Harness to run incumbent tools against corpus cases.
decision_needed: Which implementations (incumbent archivers/libraries, versions) populate the matrix and how is it kept current?

statement: Prior research found no one publishes an observed-outcome matrix: corpora publish what should happen, not what does; such a matrix would have caught the registry misclassification.
research_needed: Re-survey for any published observed-outcome matrices.

statement: Ship a standalone verifier that runs the corpus against any implementation and produces a machine-readable conformance report.
decision_needed: What is the verifier's implementation-under-test interface and report schema?

statement: Corpus licence clarity from day one: every case generated from format primitives, no third-party fixture bytes, published under a permissive licence so downstream projects can vendor it without legal review.
decision_needed: Which permissive licence governs the corpus?

statement: Adapter corpora must capture real-world legacy ambiguity, yet all cases must be generated from primitives with no third-party bytes; unclear whether every real-world malicious/ambiguous legacy artifact can be faithfully regenerated this way.
research_needed: Attempt to regenerate known ambiguous ZIP/tar cases from primitives and confirm identical tool behaviour.
decision_needed: Are adapter corpora bound by the no-third-party-bytes rule, and what is done when a case cannot be synthesised?

statement: The corpus is versioned with the format and is part of the release, not a test directory.
The concrete library API specification is deferred to §25.1 item 21; §19.4 fixes only the conceptual shape needed to keep §13.6 and §11.5 claims.
refines_or_supersedes: §25.1 item 21 L2553 (types, signatures, error enum deferred)
decision_needed: What are the library's concrete types, signatures and error enum?

statement: The library surface has four conceptual objects: Archive, EntryCursor, ExtractionPolicy and Reader.
Archive represents an opened archive and exposes descriptor, features, budgets, identities, fidelity report, conversion record, and an entry cursor.
EntryCursor iterates entries and declares its own complexity class per §13.6.
ExtractionPolicy holds resource budget, metadata classes to restore, special-file handling, collision handling, ownership and setuid policy, and confinement mode.
Reader is a byte-range reader over one entry's content, with a verification mode.

Complexity is visible: EntryCursor reports Sequential on STREAM layout and RandomAccess on INDEXED; asking a Sequential cursor for entry n yields a distinguishable 'requires a full pass or a repack' outcome, never a silent O(n) scan.
refines_or_supersedes: Implements §13.6 L1556
research_needed: API conformance tests for complexity class reporting.

statement: ExtractionPolicy is caller-constructed and archive-immutable; no path exists by which archive content constructs or mutates a policy (I16).
research_needed: API review / type-level enforcement check.

statement: Verification state is carried, never inferred: each Reader result states whether bytes were verified against a chunk digest, against a Merkle slice rooted in a signed PCR, or not at all; callers cannot mistake unverified for verified (I25).
research_needed: Type-level design proving unverified bytes cannot flow as verified.

statement: Library errors are typed and carry a reason code from the §20.5 taxonomy; an error type collapsing truncated, corrupt and unsupported-feature into one variant makes I21 untestable.
The 'requires a full pass or a repack' outcome for entry-n on a Sequential cursor is not one of the six §20.5 outcome classes; its classification and reason code are unspecified.
decision_needed: Which outcome class and reason code does a Sequential-cursor random-access request return?

statement: Reader distinguishes three verification states (chunk digest, signed-PCR Merkle slice, none) while §20.5 offers only OK with an optional UNVERIFIED qualifier; how chunk-digest-only (unsigned) verification is reported is undefined.
decision_needed: How do the three Reader verification states map onto OK / OK+UNVERIFIED and reason codes?

statement: Mount/FUSE is deliberately Ecosystem rather than Core: a mount is a filesystem with its own correctness, security and platform obligations that would otherwise be smuggled into v1; it follows once the random-access model is proven.
refines_or_supersedes: §22.4 L2415 disposition 4 Extension; §24 item 1 L2503
decision_needed: What milestone counts as 'random-access model proven' to begin mount work?

statement: Once the random-access model is proven, a mount is claimed to be a straightforward consumer of it, and the surface that makes a chunked seekable archive feel magical.
research_needed: Prototype FUSE/WinFsp/macFUSE over INDEXED layout, including metadata mapping and latency.

statement: Language bindings follow one working implementation, not the specification, because bindings written against a spec encode assumptions the implementation later contradicts.
Entrybound uses four distinct extensibility mechanisms, each for a different job, because formats fail to evolve when one mechanism is used for everything.
Archive-level capability is expressed by a three-tier feature bitmap: incompat, ro_compat, compat.
refines_or_supersedes: Tier semantics fixed; bit assignments deferred to §25.1 item 14 L2546

statement: A reader that does not implement an incompat feature MUST refuse the archive.
A reader that does not implement a ro_compat feature MAY read the archive but MUST NOT write it.
A reader that does not implement a compat feature may ignore it entirely.

ro_compat forbids 'writing', but Entrybound has no append-in-place and all modifications are full rewrites (repack); which operations (repack, repack --add, key add/remove, adding signatures, strip-provenance) count as writing is undefined.
decision_needed: Which tool operations are forbidden when an unimplemented ro_compat feature is present?

statement: The three-tier bitmap from the most-deployed Linux filesystem is claimed to be the only shape that can express 'you may read but not write', enabling old readers to safely consume newer archives.
evidence_in_source: reference to unnamed filesystem, no citation
research_needed: Primary citation (ext4 superblock feature fields) and survey of alternative shapes.

statement: A refinement from a related filesystem design, deriving the supported-feature mask from the highest defined feature rather than enumerating it, is called 'worth copying' but not stated as normative.
decision_needed: Is derived (highest-defined-feature) supported-mask computation normative for implementations or only advice?

statement: Writers adopt a disabled/enabled/active tri-state: a feature may be enabled in a writer without being active in an archive, becoming an incompat requirement only when it first changes the layout.

Because a feature becomes active only when it changes layout, the archive's feature-bit set depends on content and planner choices; interaction with declared determinism levels (§12) and reproducibility across planner versions is unspecified.
research_needed: Test that identical inputs under identical planner IDs always activate identical feature sets.
decision_needed: Is the active feature set part of the determinism contract?

statement: Every metadata item carries a criticality bit (§10.3), the pattern of image chunk types, certificate extensions and signature subpackets, scaling to an unbounded extension vocabulary without a central capability registry.
refines_or_supersedes: Refers to §10.3

statement: If the serialisation choice cannot carry a criticality bit, a list of critical item names (signature-format style) is noted as an alternative; the choice depends on §25 serialisation.
refines_or_supersedes: §25.1 item 1 L2533 serialisation encoding deferred
decision_needed: Bit or critical-name list, once the manifest serialisation is chosen?

statement: The safe-to-copy bit is adopted: it tells a rewriting tool whether an unknown metadata item may survive a repack, avoiding either dropping all unknowns or preserving invalid ones.

When repack drops an unknown not-safe-to-copy item, AUX (and thus content_binding) presumably changes and signatures go stale; required reporting, refusal and signature handling for such drops are unspecified.
decision_needed: Must repack refuse, warn, or require --drop-signatures when discarding not-safe-to-copy unknown items?

statement: Every reserved bit and field must be zero, and a reader must error if any is set, because a set bit could signal a new field that would cause later data to be misparsed.
Whether a set reserved bit yields UNSUPPORTED (possibly a newer minor version's field) or NONCONFORMING (violates a rule) is not stated.
decision_needed: Which outcome class does a non-zero reserved bit produce, and does it depend on format minor version?

statement: Codecs and transforms are registry-gated (§5.8); an unknown codec identifier is an incompat feature, so it fails closed at open time rather than decode time.
Failing closed at open time requires every used codec ID to be declared before payload; how a STREAM-layout writer, whose planner picks codecs while streaming, declares them up front is unspecified.
research_needed: Prototype streaming writer with pre-declared codec set.
decision_needed: Must STREAM writers pre-declare a codec superset, or can unknown codecs be discovered at decode time in STREAM layout?

statement: Entrybound fails closed on unknown critical features and unknown codecs, and fails open only on explicitly optional items, which remain covered by digests and signatures.

One major proprietary archive format's specification mandates that readers skip unknown record types without interrupting, so older readers silently produce wrong output if new records change interpretation.
refines_or_supersedes: Basis for §22.2 L2371 RAR5 'mandated open' and §22.4 L2421 reject
research_needed: Primary citation from RAR5 technote text.

statement: Another mainstream format's 'version needed to extract' field is advisory and universally ignored, its extra-field mechanism is designed to be skipped, and it has no critical-feature bitmap.
research_needed: Survey of ZIP implementations' handling of version-needed-to-extract.

statement: Feature bits are allocated from a central registry per tier; bits are never reused and retired bits stay retired.
refines_or_supersedes: Assignments deferred to §25.1 item 14 L2546

statement: Codec IDs come from a central registry with reserved experimental and vendor ranges; registration requires a normative reference, test vectors and a stated licence.
refines_or_supersedes: Consistent with §5.8 criteria L639
decision_needed: What are the sizes/boundaries of experimental and vendor codec-ID ranges?

statement: Transform IDs follow the codec-ID registry rules and additionally declare a reversibility class (§5.5).
Metadata names are closed in core. and platform namespaces and open in x-; x- names must be reverse-DNS.
refines_or_supersedes: Consistent with §10.2a closed namespaces enumerated (L1223)

statement: Each registered metadata name carries a type, default criticality, restorability class, and an identity-participation set naming which identity profiles include it.
refines_or_supersedes: Refines §10.2a L1223, which recorded only whether a name participates in identity/v1

statement: identity/v1 participation set is exactly {core.executable}.
refines_or_supersedes: Consistent with §8.3 L930 and §10.2a L1227

statement: identity/strict-v1 participation set is {core.executable, core.mtime, posix.mode, posix.uname, posix.gname, posix.hardlink_group}.
refines_or_supersedes: Enumerates §8.3 L934 ('full mode bits, ownership names, mtime, hardlink_group')

statement: x- metadata names may never participate in any identity profile, otherwise a writer could change LAI by inventing a name (writer-controlled identity).

identity/strict-v1 includes only POSIX metadata (names, not numeric uid/gid) and no Windows or macOS metadata, so 'the same tree, exactly' is POSIX-scoped; cross-platform strict identity is unaddressed.
decision_needed: Should numeric uid/gid or Windows/macOS metadata participate in any registered strict identity profile?

statement: Recipient stanza types come from a central registry plus vendor range; unknown stanza types are ignored but MAC-covered (§9.3).
refines_or_supersedes: A fail-open exception to §20.2 L2196; refers to §9.3

statement: When an archive's only usable recipients use unknown stanza types, ignoring them leaves the reader unable to decrypt; whether this reports UNSUPPORTED (with stanza type) or a generic no-matching-recipient is unspecified.
decision_needed: What outcome class and detail does a reader emit when only unknown stanza types are present?

statement: Identity profiles are centrally registered and frozen once published.
Planner IDs are centrally registered and frozen forever (§5.7).
refines_or_supersedes: Refers to §5.7

statement: Seven central registries are required (feature bits, codec IDs, transform IDs, metadata names, stanza types, identity profiles, planner IDs), but the registry operator, governance, publication location and change process are unspecified.
research_needed: Review IANA/PRONOM-style governance models for suitability.
decision_needed: Who operates and governs Entrybound's registries, and under what process are entries allocated?

statement: The deprecation mechanism is written into v1 because archive files outlive software and the 'everyone updates' model of live protocols is unavailable.
A retired feature or suite keeps its identifier forever; identifiers are never reused.

A reader encountering a retired-but-known identifier decodes normally and emits a DEPRECATED diagnostic naming the identifier, the retiring version and recommended replacement; it does not refuse (a 2031 archive must open in 2051).

Readers must decode retired identifiers without refusal, but for cryptographic suites retired because they are broken, silently decrypting/accepting signatures with only a DEPRECATED diagnostic may be unsafe; no security-driven exception is stated.
research_needed: Security review of retired-suite acceptance semantics (e.g., broken signature scheme verification results).
decision_needed: Should retired-because-broken crypto suites decode normally, decode with signatures reported untrusted, or be policy-refusable?

statement: A writer refuses to create archives using a retired identifier unless explicitly forced, and records the override.
decision_needed: Where is a forced-retired-identifier override recorded (descriptor, conversion record, AUX-covered section)?

statement: `entrybound inspect --deprecations` reports every retired construct in an archive, making migration a queryable maintenance task.
refines_or_supersedes: Option is absent from the §17.4 inspect synopsis L1896-1903
decision_needed: Add --deprecations to the §17.4 inspect option list?

statement: A retirement is a specification revision with a stated date, and the specification carries a permanent retirement table.
The DEPRECATED diagnostic is neither one of the six outcome classes nor declared a qualifier like UNVERIFIED; how it composes with OK and its reason-code form are unspecified.
decision_needed: Is DEPRECATED a qualifier on OK, a separate diagnostic channel, or an outcome class?

statement: The diagnostics taxonomy is part of the format, not of an implementation, because I21 (distinguishing truncation, corruption, unsupported) and I25 (report unverified) are untestable unless outcomes are named.
There are six top-level outcome classes, each carrying a stable reason code and a machine-readable detail record.
Outcome OK means conforming and verified.
Outcome UNSUPPORTED means well-formed but requires a feature the reader lacks; detail names the feature bit, tier and codec ID.
Outcome TRUNCATED means a well-formed prefix whose declared length exceeds actual; detail gives declared length, actual length and last intact entry.
Outcome CORRUPT means structure or digest mismatch; detail gives section, chunk, expected and actual digest.
Outcome NONCONFORMING means a normative rule is violated; detail gives invariant, entry and byte offset.
Outcome POLICY_REFUSED means conforming but exceeding the caller's policy; detail gives budget field, declared value and policy value.
UNVERIFIED is a qualifier that may accompany OK, not an outcome class; 'read and fine' and 'read but could not check' must never be the same answer.
Reason codes are stable across versions and form part of the conformance corpus's expected output: each case asserts which code a rejection carries, not merely that it is rejected.

Only six classes are defined; the concrete reason-code enumeration and the precedence when several classes apply (e.g., truncated archive also using an unsupported feature, or corrupt and over-budget) are not specified.
refines_or_supersedes: §25.1 item 21 L2553 says §20.5 'fixes the reason-code taxonomy'
decision_needed: What is the full reason-code registry and the outcome precedence order?

statement: TRUNCATED relies on a declared length exceeding actual, but a truncated STREAM-layout archive may have lost the footer that declares total length; how truncation is distinguished from corruption there is unclear.
research_needed: Corpus cases truncating STREAM archives at every structural boundary.
decision_needed: How is TRUNCATED detected when the length-declaring footer is itself missing?

statement: POLICY_REFUSED detail requires a declared value, but streaming archives set BudgetDeclared=false; the outcome when a policy limit is exceeded mid-read without a declared budget is unspecified.
decision_needed: What class/detail is reported when an undeclared budget is exceeded during streaming decode?

statement: A conforming decoder for the baseline feature and codec set must be implementable from the specification and test vectors alone by a competent engineer without access to Entrybound source code.
research_needed: Clean-room implementation by an engineer with only spec and vectors.

statement: Decoder longevity is a hard constraint on §5.8 and §20.3: it excludes any codec whose only specification is its implementation and caps baseline set size.
refines_or_supersedes: Constrains §5.8 criteria L639 and §25.1 item 3

statement: The 2026 data-compression challenge's <=1 MB decompressor constraint is cited as the right instinct: a format whose decoder cannot be rebuilt is not archival regardless of ratio.
refines_or_supersedes: Also cited at §4.9 L479 as 'AIT' challenge
research_needed: Primary citation; decide whether a comparable numeric cap applies to Entrybound baseline.
decision_needed: Does Entrybound adopt a numeric decoder-size cap?

statement: The normative specification must be published at a stable, archived, versioned URL.
decision_needed: Where and how is the spec archived (e.g., DOI, standards body, web archive)?

statement: The conformance corpus is published alongside the specification (§19.3).
At least one independent implementation must exist before v1.0 is declared stable, since a second implementation is the only real test that the spec says what its authors think.
refines_or_supersedes: Matrix §22.2 L2377 'required before v1.0'; §5.8 L639 codec criterion
research_needed: Plan and resource an independent implementation.
decision_needed: Who builds the independent implementation and by when?

statement: What qualifies as 'independent' (different team, language, no shared crates or codec libraries) and its required scope (full reader/writer vs baseline decoder) are undefined.
decision_needed: What independence criteria and feature scope must the second implementation meet for v1.0?

statement: The format must have no structural external dependency (§4.9).
refines_or_supersedes: Refers to §4.9

statement: Rejected: shipping the decompressor inside the archive as sandboxed VM bytecode (zpaq-style), because every decoder must implement a VM and the security surface becomes the sandbox, a less-understood bug class that must stay correct for thirty years.
refines_or_supersedes: §22.4 L2420 disposition 5 Reject

statement: Chosen instead: a small frozen baseline, a registry with mandatory test vectors, and a size budget that keeps the baseline honest.
refines_or_supersedes: Size budget value not stated (see §19.2 L2115)

statement: Adoption follows five stages: (1) better tools on legacy archives, (2) internal .eb use with legacy output, (3) dual publishing, (4) Entrybound-aware consumers prefer .eb, (5) legacy artifacts become optional fallback.
evidence_in_source: strategy, no market data in this section
research_needed: Adoption/market validation per stage (see Research I-III).

statement: Stage 1: `entrybound convert --strict --dry-run` acts as a ZIP and tar conformance checker reporting every ambiguity with byte offsets and authorities.
refines_or_supersedes: Consistent with §14.3 L1630 and §17.5 L1945

statement: Nothing in the ecosystem does ZIP/tar ambiguity checking with offsets and authorities today; the closest equivalents are private per-gatekeeper validators that disagree.
research_needed: Survey existing ZIP/tar linting and validation tools (e.g., zipdetails, registry validators, scanners).

statement: Stage 1: `entrybound verify legacy.zip --canonical` supports artifact auditing.

--canonical checks canonical-form conformance of the native model's single serialisation; what canonical form means for a legacy ZIP input is undefined, and the §17.3 verify synopsis accepts only <archive.eb>.
decision_needed: Define canonical-form checking semantics for legacy inputs, or restate Stage 1 as convert --strict?

statement: Stage 1: `entrybound inspect legacy.tar.gz --fidelity` answers 'what would I lose'.
refines_or_supersedes: §17.4 inspect synopsis L1896 shows only <archive.eb> input
decision_needed: Does inspect accept legacy inputs directly (implicit dry-run import)?

statement: Stage 1: `entrybound diff a.zip b.zip --logical` compares two archives semantically rather than by bytes.
refines_or_supersedes: §17.4 L1925 lists archive-vs-archive, archive-vs-directory and archive-vs-legacy, not legacy-vs-legacy
decision_needed: Is legacy-vs-legacy diff in v1 scope?

statement: Stage 1 requires no adoption commitment, produces immediate value, builds the adapters and observation model everything later depends on, and earns credibility for the native format.
research_needed: User/gatekeeper demand validation for legacy conformance checking.

statement: Sequencing: the Stage 1 legacy tooling is the vehicle that builds the adapters and Legacy Observation Model on which later native stages depend.
Stage 2: a build pipeline packs to .eb for caching, incremental builds and integrity, then exports .zip or .tar.zst at publication; the .eb never leaves the organisation.
research_needed: Deterministic export fidelity and speed in CI workloads.

statement: Sidecar manifests (§15.4) let a project compute and publish Entrybound identities for artifacts it still ships in legacy form.
refines_or_supersedes: Refers to §15.4

statement: Stage 3 dual publishing: release.eb alongside release.zip from one semantic source, both deterministic, with the legacy artifact's receipt naming the LAI it derives from (§15.3); .eb is source of truth and legacy is a rendering.
refines_or_supersedes: Refers to §15.3
research_needed: Byte-reproducibility of legacy exports across tool versions/platforms.

statement: Stage 4: Entrybound-aware installers, CI runners and package managers take .eb and gain partial retrieval, verified ranges, better ratio and authenticated encryption, while others take legacy; nobody is broken.
research_needed: Ratio benchmarks vs published legacy artifacts; consumer integration pilots.

statement: Stage 5: legacy artifacts become an optional fallback, published on request rather than by default.
Stage 1 switching-cost mechanism: command aliases c, x, t, create, extract so muscle memory transfers.
refines_or_supersedes: Consistent with §17.7 L1984 alias mapping

statement: Stage 1-2 mechanism: one-command conversion with a receipt, making migration auditable and therefore approvable.
Stage 2 mechanism: sidecar manifests provide Entrybound identity without changing the published artifact.
Stage 3 mechanism: deterministic dual publishing makes both artifacts reproducible from one source.
Stage 3-4 mechanism: transparent read adapters let a library consumer read .eb, .zip and .tar.* through one interface.
Stage 2-4 mechanism: CI and build-system plugins, where archives are actually created.
refines_or_supersedes: §19.1 L2104 tiers these as Ecosystem
decision_needed: Which CI/build plugins are prioritised and who maintains them?

statement: Stage 4-5 mechanism: package-manager integration, the step that makes .eb the default.
Stage 5 mechanism: OS and file-manager association for consumer-facing recognition.
A legacy archive read through the native library interface must not appear to have native guarantees; the library surfaces the source format and applied import policy on every handle.
--strict is the default for library transparent read adapters too; a caller wanting lenient legacy reading must explicitly request it.

The §19.4 four-object library shape lists no source-format or import-policy field, and Reader verification states assume native digests; how legacy handles expose provenance and report CRC32-only integrity is unspecified.
decision_needed: How do Archive/Reader objects represent legacy source format, import policy and legacy-only integrity checks?

statement: The native format is never weakened to ease the transition.
No `..` path components for compatibility with existing tarballs.
No duplicate paths in the native format, even though some ZIPs have them.
No unauthenticated encryption mode to ease migration of 7z users.
No lossy transforms to match what other archivers claim.
No fail-open unknown records so that old readers keep working.
No self-extracting executable prefix, despite user expectation.
Each refusal is acknowledged as a real adoption cost; compatibility lives at the adapter boundary (§14.5), never in the model.
refines_or_supersedes: Refers to §14.5
research_needed: Quantify adoption cost: frequency of '..', duplicate paths, SFX, unauthenticated encryption in real-world archive corpora.

statement: All §22 comparison entries describe architectural capability, not measured performance, since the Entrybound implementation does not yet exist; a matrix showing an unbuilt system winning is not evidence.
research_needed: Benchmark and conformance measurements of the implementation against every Entrybound cell once built.

statement: Where an incumbent is superior, one of five dispositions is assigned: Match natively, Exceed, Incorporate via planner/codec, Support via extension (registry-gated), Deliberately reject with justification.

Matrix fairness rules: every format, including Entrybound, is scored at its best configuration per row with the configuration named; Entrybound's profile-dependent rows are marked; rows where its best configuration precludes another capability are marked partial.
refines_or_supersedes: Corrects an earlier draft that scored Entrybound per-row best against incumbents scored once

statement: Fairness-rule application appears uneven: density (dense/extreme), compression speed (fast), and decompression speed are full marks while dense/extreme lookback degrades parallel decode and random access; decompression speed has no profile qualifier.
research_needed: Measure decode speed and access granularity per profile to justify each mark.
decision_needed: Should density/speed/random-access cells be marked partial or profile-qualified under the stated fairness rule?

statement: Per-entry codec choice: Entrybound claims full support, per chunk group; ZIP full; DwarFS full per category; 7z partial per folder; RAR5 and Apple AA partial; tar+codec, zstd, gzip, xz, squashfs/EROFS and OCI absent by design.
research_needed: Verify incumbent cells against primary specs; demonstrate per-chunk-group codec choice in implementation.

statement: Content-directed codec selection: only Entrybound and DwarFS are marked full; all other incumbents absent.
research_needed: Verify DwarFS categoriser behaviour; measure planner gains over fixed-codec baselines.

statement: Reversible preprocessing transforms: Entrybound full plus mandatory verification; 7z and xz full (filters), DwarFS full, RAR5 partial; others absent.
research_needed: Verify RAR5 filter set and DwarFS transforms; measure transform benefit and verification cost.

statement: Archival compression density: Entrybound full in dense/extreme; tar+codec (xz/zstd-22), 7z, RAR5, zstd (--ultra --long), xz and DwarFS full; ZIP, squashfs, Apple, OCI partial; gzip absent.

statement: Deterministic output: Entrybound full with four declared levels; tar best-in-class; zstd and xz with pinned params, squashfs (-repro), DwarFS, OCI full; ZIP (flags) and gzip (-n) partial; 7z, RAR5, Apple undocumented.

statement: POSIX metadata fidelity: Entrybound full; tar best-in-class; squashfs/EROFS, DwarFS, Apple AA, OCI full; ZIP (extra fields), 7z, RAR5 partial; stream compressors absent.

statement: Windows metadata fidelity: only Entrybound full; tar (vendor keys), 7z (attrs), RAR5, OCI partial; ZIP, squashfs, DwarFS, Apple absent.

statement: macOS metadata fidelity: Entrybound full; Apple AA best-in-class; ZIP partial (sidecar dir) and tar partial; 7z, RAR5, filesystems and OCI absent.

statement: Declared metadata loss: only Entrybound (Fidelity Report); every incumbent absent by design.
research_needed: Verify no incumbent emits a loss report (e.g., bsdtar warnings, 7z warnings).

statement: Streaming creation: Entrybound full unencrypted but absent for encrypted archives in v1; ZIP, tar, zstd, gzip, xz, Apple AA, OCI full; RAR5 partial; 7z, squashfs, DwarFS absent.

statement: Encrypted streaming creation is not provided in v1; only unencrypted archives can be created in streaming fashion.

research_needed: Identify what blocks encrypted streaming (budgets, padding, key-derived boundaries, commitment) and prototype.
decision_needed: Will encrypted streaming creation be added post-v1, and what design change enables it?

statement: Streaming extraction: Entrybound full; tar, zstd, gzip, xz, Apple, OCI full; ZIP, 7z, RAR5 partial; filesystems n/a.
research_needed: Measure bounded-memory streaming extraction of INDEXED and encrypted archives.

statement: Random entry access: Entrybound full for INDEXED but absent for STREAM until repacked; ZIP, squashfs, DwarFS, Apple, OCI full; 7z (folder), RAR5 (non-solid), xz (block) partial; tar, zstd, gzip absent.
research_needed: Measure random-access latency and granularity per profile.

statement: Partial/range retrieval: Entrybound, Apple AA and OCI full; ZIP, zstd (seekable), xz partial; 7z, RAR5, squashfs, DwarFS absent; tar and gzip absent by design.
research_needed: Verify squashfs/DwarFS range-retrieval marks (random-access images scored absent).

statement: Remote HTTP-range access: Entrybound full, 'native'; OCI full; ZIP (ad hoc) and zstd partial; Apple undocumented; others absent.
research_needed: Measure request counts/latency for remote INDEXED reads.

statement: Remote HTTP-range access is scored 'native', yet §24 says Entrybound defines no transport protocol and specifies no fetch protocol in v1; what 'native' guarantees (fetch strategy, index location, request bounds) is unclear.
decision_needed: What minimum remote-access behaviour (index discovery, range coalescing, verification) is normative for 'native' HTTP-range support?

statement: Verified partial reads: Entrybound full via Merkle slices against signed PCR; Apple AEA partial (HMAC chain); OCI partial (flat digests); all others absent.

statement: Parallel compression: Entrybound full; nearly every incumbent full; ZIP partial.
refines_or_supersedes: Concurrency model deferred §25.1 item 20 L2552
research_needed: Show parallel compression preserves deterministic-mode output.

statement: Parallel decompression: Entrybound full at lookback 0, partial for dense/extreme; xz (blocks), squashfs, DwarFS, Apple, OCI full; ZIP, 7z, RAR5, zstd (frames) partial; tar (gzip) and gzip absent.

statement: Format-declared resource bounds: Entrybound full with 8 fields 'when declared' (§4.2); 7z (dict size), RAR5 (KDF only), zstd (window), xz partial; Apple absent; others absent by design.

statement: Safe extraction guaranteed by format: Entrybound full; ZIP, tar, 7z, RAR5, Apple AA, OCI absent by design; stream compressors and filesystems n/a.
research_needed: Cross-OS confinement feasibility (symlink races, TOCTOU, case-insensitive collisions, Windows reparse points); a format cannot by itself guarantee implementation-level safety.

statement: Traversal structurally impossible: Entrybound full in the model, with target-hostile bytes a detected class (P8); ZIP, tar, 7z, RAR5, Apple, OCI absent.
research_needed: Fuzzing and formal check of LogicalPath rules; OS-specific hostile-name catalogue.

statement: Duplicate or prefix-conflicting paths impossible: Entrybound full via P4 and P6; ZIP, tar, 7z, RAR5, Apple, OCI absent.

statement: Parser-differential resistance: Entrybound full; ZIP absent (bold); RAR5 absent; tar, 7z, Apple, OCI partial; zstd, gzip, xz, squashfs, DwarFS full.
research_needed: Differential fuzzing between reference and independent implementations; corpus observed-outcome results.

statement: Fail-closed on unknown features: Entrybound full (three-tier plus criticality); RAR5 absent (mandated open); ZIP, tar absent; 7z codec-only; zstd (reserved bits), gzip, xz (+flags CRC), squashfs (bitmap), OCI (media type) full; DwarFS and Apple (profile ID) partial.

statement: Corruption localisation: Entrybound full; RAR5, xz (index), DwarFS, Apple full; tar (uncompressed), zstd, squashfs, OCI partial; ZIP, 7z, gzip absent.

statement: Error correction/recovery: Entrybound absent by design (§22.5); RAR5 best-in-class; Apple AA full (ECC field); all others absent.

research_needed: Verify whether Apple AA/AEA actually ships in-format ECC.

statement: Diagnostics quality: Entrybound full via inspect/explain; zstd, xz, DwarFS full; tar, RAR5, gzip, squashfs, OCI partial; ZIP, 7z, Apple absent.
research_needed: Define diagnostics-quality criteria and run usability evaluation.

statement: Normative specification: Entrybound full; ZIP, tar (ISO/IEEE), zstd and gzip (RFC), xz, OCI full; RAR5 (vendor note) and squashfs partial; DwarFS absent; 7z (source note) and Apple AA (none published) absent by design.

statement: Official conformance corpus: Entrybound shipped at v1; OCI full (dist-spec only); zstd partial; all others absent.
research_needed: Verify zstd and OCI conformance suites; survey others.

statement: Multiple independent implementations: Entrybound 'required before v1.0'; ZIP, tar, zstd, gzip, xz, squashfs, OCI full; 7z partial; RAR5 decode only; DwarFS and Apple AA absent.
refines_or_supersedes: Consistent with §20.6 L2247
research_needed: Track independent implementation progress.

statement: Apple AA/AEA is included as the closest architectural competitor; it already ships authenticated encryption with an encrypted index, native signing, random access and in-format error correction.
research_needed: Verify each Apple AA/AEA capability against Apple documentation and libAppleArchive behaviour.

statement: Entrybound's differentiators versus Apple AA/AEA are multi-recipient support, post-quantum KEM, a published normative spec, a conformance corpus, cross-platform metadata fidelity, and identity separation.
research_needed: Confirm Apple's recipient and spec status; validate differentiators with users.

statement: Apple AEA integrity is a hash chain over clusters rather than a tree, so authenticating cluster n implies authenticating clusters 0..n-1; hence its verified-partial-read mark is partial.
research_needed: Verify AEA cluster authentication structure.

statement: ZIP and tar lead on ubiquity (every OS and language runtime); Entrybound will not match this for years and §21 is the entire answer.
tar/pax leads today on metadata fidelity: its extended-header mechanism is excellent and an ISO/IEEE standard with decades of interop.
research_needed: Metadata round-trip comparison vs pax once implemented.

statement: RAR5 leads on error correction with Reed-Solomon recovery records covering very large fractions of protected data; nothing else ships this.
refines_or_supersedes: Contradicted by §22.2 L2373/L2379 marking Apple AA with in-format ECC
research_needed: Verify RAR5 recovery record limits and whether Apple AA ships ECC.

statement: Context-mixing and neural compressors reach about 40% below general-purpose codecs on text, at four to five orders of magnitude more time, tens of GB of memory, and licence/hardware constraints precluding shipping.
research_needed: Primary benchmark citation (e.g., enwik9/LTCB results) for the ~40% and time/memory figures.

statement: squashfs, EROFS and DwarFS lead on kernel-level mount performance because they are filesystems; Entrybound is an archive that can be mounted, which is not the same.
research_needed: Mount benchmark if FUSE integration is built.

statement: DwarFS leads peak dedup ratio on highly redundant trees; its headline ratio collapses on low-redundancy data.
research_needed: Reproduce DwarFS vs Entrybound dedup on redundant and low-redundancy corpora.

statement: §22.4 claims dispositions for every incumbent lead, yet ubiquity (ZIP/tar), peak dedup ratio (DwarFS), and Apple AEA encrypted streaming creation (where Entrybound is absent in v1) have no disposition row.
decision_needed: Add disposition rows for ubiquity, DwarFS peak dedup, and encrypted streaming creation?

statement: Per-entry codec choice (ZIP): disposition 1 Match, via per-chunk-group codecs (§5), finer than per entry.
Solid cross-file compression (7z, RAR5): disposition 1 Match, bounded, via chunk groups with declared access cost (§7.5).
research_needed: Measure ratio vs 7z solid at equivalent lookback.

statement: Instruction and delta filters (7z, xz): disposition 3 Incorporate as structural transforms (§5.5).
Long-window matching (zstd, lrzip): disposition 3 Incorporate (§5.3), with the window recorded as a decode requirement.
Trained dictionaries (zstd): disposition 1 Match, improved, as a first-class shared object (§3.6) rather than a per-file embed.
Content categorisation and similarity ordering (DwarFS): disposition 3 Incorporate (§5.2).
Deflate/JPEG reconstruction transforms: disposition 3 Incorporate (§5.5) with mandatory verification.
Streaming creation (tar): disposition 1 Match via STREAM layout (§4.1).
refines_or_supersedes: Matrix L2358 limits this to unencrypted archives in v1

statement: Random access (ZIP): disposition 2 Exceed (§13), with chunk-level access plus verified ranges.
refines_or_supersedes: Matrix L2360: only INDEXED layout; STREAM absent until repacked
research_needed: Benchmark vs ZIP central-directory access.

statement: Seekable frames (zstd-seekable): disposition 2 Exceed (§13.3), native and versioned in a stable spec rather than a contrib directory.
evidence_in_source: design mapping; claim about zstd contrib status
research_needed: Verify current status of zstd seekable format spec.

statement: Lazy pull over HTTP (eStargz, SOCI): disposition 2 Exceed (§13.5), native with no conversion step and the index inside the archive.
research_needed: Compare request efficiency with eStargz/SOCI; note §24 defines no fetch protocol.

statement: Metadata fidelity (tar/pax): disposition 2 Exceed (§10), typed and namespaced instead of vendor keywords, plus the Fidelity Report.
research_needed: Round-trip comparison vs pax.

statement: Determinism (tar with flags): disposition 2 Exceed (§12), with four declared levels and identity that survives recompression.
Encrypted headers (RAR5, 7z -mhe): disposition 2 Exceed (§4.7): default and authenticated.
refines_or_supersedes: Matrix L2347 qualifies default as INDEXED layout

statement: KDF-cost bound in the spec (RAR5): disposition 2 Exceed (§11.5), eight declared budget fields including a key-derivation cost bound.
refines_or_supersedes: Matches §4.2 L380 and §26.4 L2643 / §26.5 L2672 revision logs fixes

statement: Feature bitmaps (EROFS, ext4): disposition 1 Match (§20.1).
Journaling/versioned archive (zpaq): disposition 4 Extension, out of baseline (§24).
refines_or_supersedes: Consistent with §24 item 13 L2518 and §22.5 L2438

statement: Mount performance (squashfs, EROFS, DwarFS): disposition 4 Extension (§19.5).

decision_needed: Would any context-mixing codec ever meet extended-registry criteria?

statement: Error correction (RAR5): disposition 5 Reject (§22.5).
refines_or_supersedes: §24 item 15 L2520 'permanently refused', although listed under a 'deferred rather than refused' heading

statement: Self-extracting archives: disposition 5 Reject (§22.5).
Append-in-place (ZIP, tar, zpaq): disposition 5 Reject (§22.5).
refines_or_supersedes: Contradicts §24 item 12 L2517, which lists append-in-place as 'deferred rather than refused'
decision_needed: Is append-in-place permanently rejected (category 5) or deferred post-v1?

statement: In-archive decompressor bytecode (zpaq): disposition 5 Reject (§20.7).
Fail-open unknown records (RAR5): disposition 5 Reject (§20.2).
Unauthenticated encryption (7z, RAR5): disposition 5 Reject (§9.1).
Lossy 'lossless' recompression: disposition 5 Reject (§6.5).
Cross-tenant convergent dedup: disposition 5 Reject (§9.7).
Every category-5 refusal must be justified by an argument that refusing produces a better system, not merely a smaller one.
In-archive error-correction records are refused despite RAR5 being best-in-class.

External parity composes better: it protects any file including formats without recovery, and redundancy can be chosen and topped up after creation; redundancy is a storage-medium decision, not archive content.
research_needed: Operational/usability evidence that users will manage external parity files; compare recovery effectiveness vs RAR5 records.

statement: A recent WinRAR release fixed a heap overflow in RAR5 recovery-volume reconstruction, showing the recovery decoder is attack surface inside the archive parser.

research_needed: Primary citation (CVE ID, WinRAR version) for the heap overflow.

statement: What users actually need is precise damage assessment rather than repair; §8.7 names exactly which entries survived.
research_needed: User/incident evidence on repair vs assessment needs.

statement: Provide a normative binding for external parity artifacts so `entrybound verify --parity <file>` and `entrybound repair --parity <file>` work with an existing mature parity format as a first-class workflow.
refines_or_supersedes: Consistent with §17.2 L1814, L1827-1831

statement: The external parity format is not named and the binding mechanism (what identity the parity artifact binds to, whether signed, how repaired output is verified) is unspecified.
research_needed: Evaluate PAR2/PAR3 and similar formats for maturity, licence and Rust support.
decision_needed: Which parity format is bound, and how is a parity artifact bound to an archive (PCI, LAI, signature)?

statement: Self-extracting archives are refused: an executable prefix is the canonical prefix-confusion and polyglot substrate (§11.4) and asks users to run untrusted executables; refusal removes a vulnerability class at the cost of convenience.
Append-in-place is refused: the model has one manifest and one declared total length; appending needs a second manifest (violating I1) or a rewrite, which is repack.
refines_or_supersedes: Contradicts §24 item 12 L2517 'deferred rather than refused'
decision_needed: Resolve category (5 Reject vs deferred) for append-in-place.

statement: Several of the highest-value ambiguity cases in the ZIP corpus are appended-archive artifacts: two central directories, trailing data, orphaned entries and stale indexes.
research_needed: Enumerate corpus cases and their prevalence.

statement: `entrybound repack --add` provides adding entries via a full rewrite that preserves every invariant, producing a complete conforming archive with one manifest and one declared length.
refines_or_supersedes: Operation table §8.1 L905
research_needed: Measure full-rewrite cost for large archives (vs append workloads like logs/backups).
decision_needed: Is full-rewrite cost acceptable for very large archives, or is a chunk-reuse fast path required?

statement: repack --add does not preserve LAI, since the entry set changes (§8.1); the command reports the new identity rather than implying continuity.
For incremental updates, external content references (§15.4) let a new archive reference a base without copying it, claimed better than append because the result is complete and verifiable.
research_needed: Usability and failure-mode study of base-chain dependence (missing base, base substitution).

statement: The versioned-log model (append-only journal with rollback to any prior state) is category 4, a plausible future extension and a v1 non-goal rather than a permanent refusal.
refines_or_supersedes: Consistent with §24 item 13 L2518
decision_needed: Under what conditions would a versioned-journal extension be designed?

statement: Entrybound is not superior on any single axis to the best specialist: stream compressors are faster, context-mixing archivers smaller given days and 30 GiB, purpose-built read-only filesystems mount faster.
System-level claim: for any combination of capabilities a real project needs, Entrybound is the only system providing all at once, without the project needing to know the combination in advance.
research_needed: Falsification exercise per §23.2 combinations with a built implementation; user-need survey of capability combinations.

statement: 'Without knowing the combination in advance' conflicts with layout/profile choices fixed at creation: STREAM lacks random access until repack, encrypted archives cannot be stream-created in v1, and dense/extreme lookback limits parallel decode.
decision_needed: Should the superiority claim be narrowed, or must post-hoc conversions (repack) be treated as satisfying it?

statement: Unserved combination: random access and strong compression; ZIP gives weak ratio, 7z solid gives no random access.
refines_or_supersedes: Entrybound dense/extreme lookback reduces access granularity (§22.2 L2365)
research_needed: Measure ratio vs access-granularity curve (§25.3 L2572) against ZIP and 7z.

statement: Unserved combination: streaming creation and random access; tar has no seeking and ZIP streams awkwardly.
refines_or_supersedes: Entrybound STREAM layout lacks random access until repacked (§22.2 L2360)
research_needed: Determine whether STREAM plus later index/repack satisfies this need in practice.
decision_needed: Does Entrybound serve this combination in a single pass, or only via repack?

statement: Unserved combination: deduplication with a portable single-file archive; backup tools offer repositories, not archives.
refines_or_supersedes: Tension with §22.2 L2342, where DwarFS (a single-file image) has full chunk dedup
research_needed: Assess whether DwarFS/other single-file deduplicating images count as portable archives.

statement: Unserved combination: authenticated encryption, encrypted index and multi-recipient; Apple's encrypted archive has the first two, on one platform, without a published spec.
research_needed: Verify Apple AEA availability beyond Apple platforms and recipient model; check age/OpenPGP-over-tar combinations.

statement: Unserved combination: reproducible builds with preserved metadata; content-addressed store formats discard metadata and tar preserves metadata without stable identity.
research_needed: Validate with reproducible-builds community practice.

statement: Unserved combination: a signature that survives recompression; only container image layers offer it.
research_needed: Survey signing schemes over logical content (e.g., OCI diff_id, sigstore over tar content).

statement: Unserved combination: verified partial download in general; only container lazy-pull formats offer it within that ecosystem.
refines_or_supersedes: §22.2 L2363 also marks Apple AEA partial
research_needed: Survey verified range download tooling outside OCI.

statement: Unserved combination: declared resource bounds before decompression; no incumbent offers any answer.
refines_or_supersedes: Contradicts §22.2 L2366 partial marks for 7z, RAR5, zstd, xz; Entrybound's own bounds exist only when declared (§4.2 L393)
research_needed: Reconcile with matrix; verify incumbent declared-bound fields.
decision_needed: Restate the row as 'complete declared bounds' or change matrix cells?

statement: Unserved combination: an explicit statement of what was not preserved; nothing offers it.
research_needed: Verify no incumbent emits machine-readable loss reports.

statement: Unserved combination: post-quantum confidentiality for long-lived archives; nothing in any archive format offers it.
research_needed: Survey 2026 PQ support in archivers and file-encryption tools used with archives.

statement: Of ten combinations, three (declared resource bounds, statement of what was not preserved, post-quantum confidentiality) have no answer in any archive format; the rest have partial answers confined to one ecosystem or platform.
refines_or_supersedes: Declared-bounds 'no answer' conflicts with §22.2 L2366
research_needed: Independent verification of each row.

statement: Content-addressed chunks as the physical unit yield dedup, random access, parallel decompression, verified ranges, corruption localisation, partial retrieval, resumability and content sharing subsuming hard links; file-unit formats cannot retrofit these.
research_needed: Resumability is claimed but not specified in this slice; validate each benefit in implementation.
decision_needed: Is resumable (interrupted) pack/unpack/download a specified capability, and where?

statement: Three signed roots separate content identity, physical arrangement and declared fidelity, making recompression, re-chunking, re-encryption, layout conversion and index rebuilding non-events.
refines_or_supersedes: Consistent with §8.0 L879 'three signed roots'
research_needed: Formal model of which bindings each operation invalidates (cf. §9.6 L1117).

statement: `repack --profile extreme` on a signed archive must not invalidate the author's content signature; the physical binding goes stale and says so (§9.6).
refines_or_supersedes: Consistent with §9.6 L1117

statement: Separating logical from physical identity allows reproducibility to coexist with non-deterministic encryption.
research_needed: Demonstrate LAI/AUX reproducibility across re-encryptions.

statement: One authority per fact with everything declared before payload structurally eliminates thirteen historical vulnerability classes (§11.2) and enables strict parsing, a meaningful corpus, and agreeing independent implementations.
refines_or_supersedes: Refers to §11.2 L1372 thirteen classes
research_needed: Security review of each claimed structural elimination.

statement: 'Everything declared before payload' conflicts with STREAM layout, where manifest records follow the chunk data they describe and budgets may be undeclared (BudgetDeclared=false).
decision_needed: Restate the principle with STREAM-layout exceptions, and confirm which vulnerability-class eliminations still hold for STREAM?

statement: Cost: no ecosystem, total at v1; mitigated by §21, with Stage 1 delivering value at zero adoption.
Cost: chunking overhead on tiny archives is real, a few hundred bytes of framing and index.
research_needed: Measure container overhead for 0-1 KB inputs vs ZIP, gzip, tar.gz.

statement: The planner degenerates to a single chunk for small inputs.
decision_needed: What input-size threshold triggers single-chunk degeneration, and is it planner-ID frozen?

statement: Cost: chunk independence costs a few percent of ratio versus solid, mitigated by shared dictionaries, similarity ordering and the lookback dial.
refines_or_supersedes: Echoes §13.4 L1543
research_needed: Measure ratio loss vs solid 7z/xz across corpora and lookback values.

statement: Cost: verification adds one extra decode pass over transformed data at write time, small next to the compression search it accompanies.
research_needed: Measure verification overhead, especially in fast profile where search is minimal.

statement: Cost: encrypted-archive padding costs storage that is bounded and declared; an opt-out exists and is recorded as a declared leak.
refines_or_supersedes: Bucket schedule deferred §25.1 item 13 L2545
research_needed: Measure padding overhead per candidate bucket schedule and leakage reduction.

statement: Entrybound has genuinely more concepts than ZIP, but the CLI hides them all; `pack` and `unpack` need no flags.
research_needed: Usability testing of flagless pack/unpack with novice users.

statement: Cost: the specification and corpus are months of real work, and are also what makes the format survive (§19.3).
research_needed: Effort planning for spec and corpus given 23 deferred design items (§25.1).

statement: Every future feature request is judged by whether it can be provided without violating a §3.9 invariant: if yes, say where and add it; if no, name the invariant and argue why keeping it yields a better system.
§22.4 is claimed to answer the feature-request test for every capability any incumbent has today, with §22.5 doing the hard half.
refines_or_supersedes: See gaps: §22.3 ubiquity/DwarFS dedup and encrypted streaming creation lack §22.4 rows
research_needed: Completeness audit of §22.4 against §22.2 and §22.3.
